physicalNotes: Radius 0.3058761 Jupiter radii from Polanski et al. 2024 (2024ApJS..272...32P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJS..272...32P/abstract): 21,867.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Polanski et al. 2024 (2024ApJS..272...32P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJS..272...32P/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 0.02202446 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Osborn et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523.3069O), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname OSBORN_ET_AL__2023): P 52.563491 d
sources.shape: Polanski et al. 2024 (2024ApJS..272...32P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POLANSKI_ET_AL__2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.269 au and stellar radius 0.9593 solar radii; Polanski et al. 2024 (2024ApJS..272...32P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POLANSKI_ET_AL__2024): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.290877 with its a/R* 60.2978 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: Polanski et al. 2024 (2024ApJS..272...32P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname POLANSKI_ET_AL__2024): e 0
sources.phase: Osborn et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523.3069O), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname OSBORN_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2458779.1919 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 5 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
